names: UCSF Mission Bay Building 23B Parking Structure
record.summary: UCSF's nine-level, 822-space Building 23B Parking Structure at 1650 3rd Street in Mission Bay, on Block 23 between 3rd and 4th Streets; the Regents approved its $23.3M budget in November 2003 with construction slated to run March 2004 to July 2005. Designed by Stanley Saitowitz/Natoma Architects, its original channel-glass facade was replaced in 2021 with IwamotoScott's 'Cellular Origami' aluminum-panel facade.

notes.accuracy_caveat: REAL -- surveyed OpenStreetMap building footprint, not a hand trace or plan estimate. Same situation as this project's other UCSF Mission Bay campus buildings: UCSF is state land, not carried in DataSF's Assessor secured tax roll (no blklot to join), so the real building footprint is the correct non-fabricated geometry.

open_questions: No source confirms the garage's actual completion date; the 2005-07 milestone above is the 2003 budget item's projected schedule, not a completion announcement -- a UC construction schedule commonly slips, so this date is flagged approximate.

The 2003 Regents item describes a nine-level, 822-space structure; this record's own geometry file cites OpenStreetMap tagging of 8 levels -- not reconciled here, since OSM levels and the Regents' 'nine levels (including a half level at the top)' description are plausibly the same building described two ways. The building's own general contractor (Overaa, added 2026-09-22) separately gives 882 stalls -- likely the as-built figure versus the Regents' pre-construction budget estimate, but not reconciled here either.
Exact capacity today (after any reconfiguration) is not confirmed by any source found, per this record's own geometry file notes.
The general contractor for the original 2004-2005 construction was not identified in this pass.
